seen.cipher: Finding aid: 'correspondence (often in code) between the governor's office and Senator Joseph M. Carey's office regarding the aftermath of the Johnson County War' and 'Correspondence between Governor's office and Sen. Carey (photocopies in box, originals in safe), May 30-June 22, 1892'. Seen: Western Union night messages and typed telegrams made of unconnected English words (e.g. Carey to Kirk, 30 May: 'Aulz requests go at Satisfactory disorder Extent They Connect ...'), a word-substitution with transposition. Filed with them: ah00003_114, a letter from Carey's office, 30 May 1892 ('We sent you a telegram last night in cypher ... I give you a copy of the telegram as translated: Tell Barber Secretary says his dispatch meant prisoners could be held ...'); ah00003_116-117, handwritten word-column worksheets; ah00003_118, typed plaintext 'Barber says your telegram perfectly understood ...' marked 'cypher May 31/92'; ah00003_121-122, typed plaintext of Kirk's 2 June telegram beside the cipher form (ah00003_123-124). So decipherments are written with the leaves; the 1 Jun Carey telegram (ah00003_120) and images 125-131 were not matched to plaintexts.
